title: Game day: execute auto-rollback on SLO breach scenarios + capture follow-ups
creator: Miles Thornton
description:
Goal
Execute the game day for Auto-rollback on SLO breach integration and capture concrete outcomes + follow-up work.

Links
- Confluence game day plan: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/game-days/game-day-auto-rollback-slo-breach.json
- Runbook draft (for reference during game day): sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/runbook-auto-rollback-on-slo-breach.json
- Rollout controller overview: sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/rollout-controller-slo-integration-overview.json
- Postmortem context: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/pm-2025-02-rollout-regression-missed-slo-signal.json

Participants (expected)
- Lead/facilitator: Miles Thornton (SRE)
- Control plane: Benji Okafor, Ethan Park
- Telemetry/observability: Nadia Rahman, Allison Grant, Sergio Costa
- Console/backend: Jada Williams / Chloe Martin delegate
- Oncall readiness: Rafael Mendes

Environment
- Use staging control plane + internal canary tenant(s) + one low-risk Dedicated tenant (if available)
- Use feature flag: auto_rollback_slo_enabled (scoped to canary tenants only)
- Rollout target: a test model version (synthetic) that allows controlled latency/error injection

Success criteria
- Auto-rollback triggers within policy window when latency/error breach is sustained and traffic threshold is met
- Rollback action is safe + idempotent (no repeated traffic-split thrash)
- Audit events emitted (trigger + action) and visible in audit log stream
- Console shows verdict + reason + rollback history within expected propagation delay
- Oncall has a clear, minimal workflow to confirm + escalate (runbook links from alerts + Slack notification)
- Failure modes behave as designed (monitor outage => unknown verdict with configured fail-open/fail-closed)

Scenarios to execute (minimum)
1) Latency regression during canary
- Inject p95 latency increase for a route/model pair only on canary version
- Expect verdict transitions: healthy -> warning -> breach
- Expect rollback executor to revert traffic split to prior stable
- Validate cooldown prevents immediate re-trigger if signal remains noisy after rollback

2) Error spike (5xx) during canary
- Inject elevated 5xxs for canary version only
- Expect rollback for error SLO breach
- Validate minimum traffic requirement (no rollback if request rate below threshold)

3) Monitor outage / stale monitors
- Simulate monitor API returning errors or returning stale datapoints
- Expect controller to set verdict=unknown and behave per policy (default: do not rollback on unknown)
- Ensure notifications clearly indicate monitoring outage vs real breach

4) Baseline comparison guardrail (must-be-worse-than-baseline)
- Create a situation where both baseline and canary are degraded (shared dependency issue)
- Ensure rollback does not trigger purely due to global incident if canary is not worse than baseline

5) Flapping resistance
- Create intermittent spikes near threshold to validate evaluation window + cooldown
- Confirm we don’t oscillate between rollback/no-rollback; only one rollback event per rollout step

Execution checklist (day-of)
- Confirm oncall rotation + comms channel (#incidents or #eng-oncall) and a dedicated game-day channel
- Confirm feature flags + tenant scoping
- Confirm dashboards load and have expected labels (route/model/region/tier)
- Confirm audit log sink available (internal viewer + export)
- Confirm rollback executor dry-run mode works (if used) and then enable real revert for the run

Deliverables
- Timestamped timeline of what we did + what happened
- List of issues found (with severity + owner) and corresponding follow-up tickets/PRs
- Recommendation: ready to proceed to staged rollout / not ready, and what must be fixed first

2025-02-26 (Miles Thornton): Game day executed today 10:00–12:00 PT. Summary + follow-ups below; marking ticket Done once all owners acknowledge action items.
outcomes:
Game day results (2025-02-26)

Timeline (PT)
- 10:05: Verified staging dashboards + label presence for selected route/model/region (us-west) + tier=hosted_internal.
- 10:15: Enabled auto rollback on canary tenant only (flag on).
- 10:25: Scenario 1 (latency): injected +250ms p95 on canary only.
  - Observed verdict change to BREACH after ~6–7 minutes (expected window=5m + monitor lag).
  - Rollback executed successfully: traffic split reverted from 20% canary -> 0% canary; rollout step marked “rolled back.”
  - Audit events emitted: AUTO_ROLLBACK_TRIGGERED + ROLLOUT_TRAFFIC_SPLIT_REVERTED (validated in audit viewer).
  - Console displayed verdict and rollback history, but the reason text was truncated (see Issue #3).
- 10:55: Scenario 2 (error): injected 5xx spike on canary only.
  - Rollback triggered correctly.
  - Confirmed minimum traffic guardrail works: when we dropped RPS below threshold, verdict still showed BREACH but executor did NOT rollback (correct).
- 11:20: Scenario 3 (monitor outage/staleness): simulated monitor API timeout + stale datapoints.
  - Found bug: controller treated “stale datapoints but last known value is bad” as BREACH and attempted rollback.
  - Expected behavior: verdict=UNKNOWN and no rollback when monitors are stale/unavailable (default fail-open for monitoring dependency).
  - Workaround during game day: disabled auto action (set action=dry_run) until scenario completed.
- 11:45: Scenario 4 (baseline comparison): degraded shared dependency for both baseline and canary.
  - Verified must-be-worse-than-baseline prevented rollback when both versions degraded similarly.
  - However, the UI did not clearly show baseline comparison status (see Issue #4).
- 12:00: Wrapped. Captured logs/trace IDs and screenshots; posted recap in #eng-oncall and #eng-platform.

What worked
- End-to-end rollback path works: evaluator -> executor -> traffic split revert -> audit -> console timeline.
- Cooldown prevented repeated rollback attempts once a rollback was already executed for the rollout step.
- Minimum traffic guardrail prevented rollback for low-volume routes.

Issues found
1) Stale monitor datapoints can incorrectly trigger rollback
- Severity: P0 (could cause false rollbacks in prod)
- Observed: stale monitors returned with old “bad” values; evaluator treated as actionable BREACH.
- Expected: treat stale as UNKNOWN; default policy should not rollback on UNKNOWN.
- Owner: Benji Okafor + Nadia Rahman
- Fix: implement explicit staleness check and propagate UNKNOWN verdict + reason.

2) Notification missing key context for oncall
- Severity: P1
- Observed: Slack notification did not include monitor identity string; runbook link was present but pointed to a draft.
- Expected: include monitor identity, policy name, verdict, and direct link to rollout step + runbook (stable URL).
- Owner: Hannah Rivera + Rafael Mendes

3) Console reason text truncation + poor readability
- Severity: P2
- Observed: rollback reason string truncated mid-sentence, and baseline comparison details not visible.
- Expected: show a structured “Reason” panel with: breached SLO, threshold, measured value, window, baseline comparison result, and staleness/unknown state.
- Owner: Felix Schneider + Chloe Martin

4) Baseline comparison not represented in verdict state
- Severity: P2
- Observed: UI showed BREACH but did not indicate “baseline worse/neutral” vs “canary worse.” Oncall had to infer from dashboards.
- Expected: verdict metadata includes comparison outcome and is shown in console.
- Owner: Jada Williams

5) Monitor lag impact not obvious in decision trace
- Severity: P3
- Observed: Decision trace logs exist but do not highlight monitor evaluation timestamp vs controller time.
- Expected: include monitor datapoint timestamps and computed “signal age” to aid debugging.
- Owner: Jordan Lee

Follow-ups created / proposed
- Created hotfix PR to prevent rollback when monitors are stale/unavailable; add UNKNOWN verdict handling (see PR reference in related work).
- Create Linear follow-up tickets (owners to file or assign):
  - (Benji/Nadia) Add staleness threshold config + UNKNOWN semantics in evaluator
  - (Hannah/Rafael) Update incident-bot formatting to include monitor identity + stable runbook link
  - (Console) Improve rollback reason UX, include baseline comparison + staleness indicators
  - (Jordan) Enhance decision trace logging with timestamps + signal age

Go/No-go recommendation
- NO-GO for expanding beyond internal canaries until staleness/UNKNOWN handling fix is in prod and verified.
- GO for continuing staged rollout after: (a) staleness fix + tests land, (b) notification context improvement merged, (c) console reason panel improvement scheduled (can be post-GA if oncall visibility is sufficient via dashboards).
